name: Handful of pale berries
description: A heap of milky white berries on a forked purple twig, picked from a bush that grows nowhere it should. They smell sweet.
notes: Fourteen berries 14 to 18 mm across heaped round a forked twig, with one leaf, 96 mm across. pearl draws the berries' milky sheen, plant-purple the twig and verdigris the leaf. Economy is empty: the berries are harvested from a strange bush, not found as loot. Food values and any harm from eating them need the food system's rules.

name: Hard-rind fruit
description: A fruit as big as a melon in a dark, ribbed rind as hard as a shell. It has to be cut open before it can be eaten.
notes: A squat egg 240 mm across and 270 mm tall with eight raised ribs, a stalk scar and five purple knobs round it. chitin-brown draws the hard rind, bark the ribs. Economy is empty: it is harvested from a strange tree, not found as loot. Cutting it open needs an unpack step with a cutting quality once the food rules exist. Box/volume x2.6 is the bounding box of a round fruit plus its ribs and knobs; the turned body is close to the reference volume.

name: Jelly fruit
description: A blue-green egg-shaped fruit that wobbles like set jelly. It gives off a sharp, sour smell.
notes: An egg 96 mm long and 68 mm thick lying on its side, with a darker core and a dry nub. `jelly-teal` draws the translucent blue-green flesh and `verdigris` the cloudy core, which shows through the jelly in the game and as a dark patch at the blunt end on the tile; a pale wet highlight runs along the top. The reference lists no material. Economy is empty: it is harvested from a strange tree, not found as loot. Box/volume x2.0 is the box round an egg.

name: Vial of pink crystal dust
description: A small corked glass vial holding a pinch of pink dust that glitters faintly when the vial is turned.
notes: Loose dust, so it is modelled in the corked glass vial a player picks up: 16 mm across and 48 mm tall, the bottom 14 mm packed with dust. The dust sits flush with the glass wall so its colour shows in the tile, which draws glass opaque. The mass is the reference's 15 g of dust; a sealed vial would add a few grams. CHECK VOLUME (x12.3): the reference's 1 ml is the dust alone. Each colour gets its own draft with a `dust` finish. A glittering or faintly glowing finish would fit better than gem-pink. Usage `Infected` stands for drops from strange creatures until a fitting tag exists.

name: Phial of refined pink crystal powder
description: A tiny round-bellied phial sealed with black wax. The fine pink powder inside sparkles even in the dark.
notes: Loose powder, so it is modelled in a tiny wax-sealed phial, 18 mm across and 36 mm tall, its belly full of powder; the round belly and wax seal set it apart from the coarser dust's corked vial. The powder sits flush with the glass so its colour shows in the tile. The mass is the reference's 5 g of powder. CHECK VOLUME (x14.4): the reference's 1 ml is the powder alone. Each colour gets its own draft with a `powder` finish. Glowing in darkness needs an emissive finish, which the palette lacks.

name: Strange pink crystal
description: A stubby six-sided crystal no bigger than a thumb tip, far heavier than it looks. A faint pink light stirs deep inside it.
notes: A double-ended hexagonal point 27 mm tall and 12 mm across, its tip tapering in four steps, with two small points jutting sideways near its foot; at the 2 mm grain the facets read as steps. Alternate faces and tip steps are a lighter `petal-pink` (slot `facet`) over `gem-pink`, so the six sides read in two tones. The reference is a tool with no qualities; it is drafted as misc until a use for it is designed. Each colour gets its own draft with `crystal`, `facet`, `point-a` and `point-b` finishes. The light in its depths needs an emissive finish, which the palette lacks. Usage `Infected` stands for drops from strange creatures.

name: Vial of crystal tonic
description: A small capped glass vial of clear liquid with a few pale crystal flecks settled in the bottom. Its label promises to steady a strained mind.
notes: A liquid, so the whole vial is one item and its 20 g includes the glass: a vial 20 mm across and 55 mm tall holding 10 ml, with a rubber stopper under a crimped aluminium cap and a white label band. The liquid and glass sit close at the 2 mm grain, so the liquid shows through the glass in stripes on the tile; both are see-through in the game. Its effect needs a status-effect rule for psychic strain, which does not exist yet. Box/volume x2.2 is the vial round its 10 ml.
